summary.text: Deep ocean water is the cold, salty water of the deep sea, beginning about 200 m below the surface.
It makes up about 90% of the oceans' volume and holds a very uniform temperature of around 0–3 °C, with a salinity near 35 parts per thousand.
In a few places it is pumped up from about 900 m for research and business, and its leftover cold can chill farm soil so crops grow where they normally could not.

facts.label: Pumped from
facts.value: About 900 m, at Hawaii's energy laboratory

items.prompt: Picture all the water in Earth's oceans. Roughly how much of it is deep ocean water?
items.explain: Deep ocean water makes up about 90% of the volume of the oceans.

items.prompt: A probe samples water 2,000 m down under a tropical sea and 2,000 m down off a cold coast. What will it most likely record?
items.explain: Deep ocean water has a very uniform temperature of around 0–3 °C.

items.prompt: Compare warm tropical surface water with cold polar surface water. Which is generally saltier?
items.explain: Warm surface water is generally saltier, while the upper layers in polar regions are cold and fresh.

items.prompt: Cold water left over from an ocean energy plant is piped under a dry field. What does it do for the crops?

options.label: Warms the soil to speed up growth
Adds sea salt that fertilizes roots
Cools the soil and draws moisture from air
Floods the field to water the plants

items.explain: Passing the cold water through underground pipes cools the soil, which cuts evaporation and even makes water condense from the air.

items.prompt: Why is water leaving an ocean thermal energy plant still colder than the air and ground around it?

options.label: The machinery chills it even further
It is mixed with ice before release
It is stored underground for months
The process needs a temperature gap to work

items.explain: These processes only work while a temperature difference remains, so the water never warms all the way to the surrounding temperature.

items.prompt: In polar seas, how does the upper layer of water compare with the deep ocean water below it?

options.label: Both cold, but upper is fresher
Exactly the same in every way
Upper is saltier, deep is fresher

items.explain: Polar upper layers are cold and fresh, while deep ocean water is cold and salty.
